Short version: I could not refute the finding. A failed bwx12 (the runner of steps L and C) leaves rx.sh with exit status 0, so go.sh continues and prints ALLDONE. The effect is a false completion report and missing or cut-short L and C data, not wrong rates, and the failure has not occurred in 230 recorded runs, so "major" is higher than the evidence supports. I rate it moderate and worth the three-line fix.

What I traced (reading the files):
- rx.sh line 20 only records the status: `wait $pid; echo "rc $? $tag utc ..." >> $out/launches.txt`. rx.sh has `set -u` and no `set -e`.
- rx.sh line 22 ends with `head -c 600 $out/stderr.txt`. That file exists after the first launch, so the exit status of rx.sh is 0.
- go.sh lines 20 and 23 test only that status (`"$RX" ... || fail ...`).
- bwx12.c has real exit(2) paths during a run, for example mmap (lines 438-440), sched_setaffinity (420-422) and the counter group read (1622-1624). A failed perf_event_open is not one of them: it prints NA and continues (1596-1601).
- ra.sh (step A) does not have this defect. It uses `set -euo pipefail`, so a failed bw_old or bw_new stops go.sh.

What I ran (local stand-ins, no workload, no ssh):
- The rx.sh I ran is byte-identical to the pinned script (sha256 d315814f..., equal to RXSHA in go.sh). A `sleep` stand-in on PATH removed the waiting.
- Stand-in bwx12 exits 2: launches.txt has `rc 2 cfwd`, rx.sh exit status 0.
- Stand-in bwx12 dies by SIGSEGV: launches.txt has `rc 139 cfwd`, rx.sh exit status 0.
- go.sh with only the SHA line changed, bwx12 failing at all 6 calls: 9 `== after` lines, `ALLDONE`, exit status 0. Same result for exit 2 and for SIGSEGV.

Does it matter for the two questions of today:
- It does not put wrong rates into the results. An empty csv makes stat_bwx.py (the bwx12 analysis script) stop with "no T rows" and status 1 (tested).
- A cut-short csv is accepted. I cut the real a6456.csv of results/w120-w120-F72d12-20261117T200231Z after part of the file. stat_bwx.py ended with status 0 and printed n=1 per kernel in place of n=2, with no warning. So a process that dies mid-run shows only as a smaller n and as the `rc` line.
- If the reverse-order step C2 (crev.spec) is the one that fails, the order control for old read against new read on bwx12 is lost, and go.sh still reports ALLDONE.
- On the shared machine, go.sh would keep loading 120 CPUs for the remaining steps after a failure that may point to a machine fault (for example a memory error on the machine with the recently unstable memory modules). This is a hypothesis about the cause, not an observed event.
- Likelihood is low. All 230 `rc` lines in results/w120-*/launches.txt are `rc 0`, and every stderr.txt there is empty. This includes the same binary with the same a6456 argument line at 7200 MT/s (F72d12, 20:02 UTC today).
- The failure is not hidden completely: rx.sh prints the non-zero `rc` line and the first 600 bytes of stderr.txt into the go.sh output. Only the exit status and the word ALLDONE are wrong.

Check of the proposed fix:
- I applied exactly the function line and the two call lines to a copy of go.sh and ran five cases. Good case: 9 `== after` lines, ALLDONE, status 0. Exit 2 at every call: stops after A1 with `FAILED: bwx12 like session 1`, status 1. SIGSEGV: same. Failure only for crev.spec: stops after L2 with `FAILED: bwx12 C session 2`, status 1. An older folder of the same name with `rc 0` plus a new failure: still stops (the newest folder is read).

- The test `= 1` relies on one launch per spec file. like.spec, cfwd.spec and crev.spec each have one line that ends with a newline (checked).
